messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Difference between MVPA in part 2 and part 5
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: Difference between MVPA in part 2 and part 5
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,
if I am correct, in part2 the full day is used (night + day) whereas in part5 estimates are splitted between night and day, and MVPA bout are calculated outside the sleep time (there can be MVPA bout during the night but only for epoch not classified as proper sleep).
As you look at MVPA of 1 minute or more (which is short period of time), it is possible that MVPA epoch are not detected as such as there are classified as sleep time.
Do you have same differencies if you use longer MVPA bouts (in that case, the epoch are less likely to be classified as sleep time)?
Regards
Séverine

Le dimanche 31 mars 2019 23:15:19 UTC+2, David a écrit :
> Hi Vincent,
>
> thanks a lot for your detailed reply. What I still don't quite understand is how I can get very different MVPA estimates when comparing the results in part2 and part 5 using the given code. As part5 should count all one minute bouts (as all other bout durations are not being calculated) I don't understand how the MVPA values of part 2 are up to twice as large.
>
> Kind regards
> David
>
> Am Sonntag, 31. März 2019 22:41:18 UTC+2 schrieb Vincent van Hees:
> > Hi David,
> >
> > Bouts are calculated with GGIR function g.getbout (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/GGIR.pdf).
> > As there is no magic universal definition of a bout, the code evolved into 4 bout metrics, from which I think number 4 is the most sensible.
> >
> > Part 2 still uses bout.metric 1 as a default while part 5 uses bout.metric 4 as a default.
> >
> > Copied from g.getbout documention: " If value=1 the code uses the MVPA bout definition as has been available since 2014 (see papers by Sabia AJE 2014 and da Silva IJE 2014). Here, the algorithm looks for 10 minute windows in which more than XX percent of the epochs are above mvpathreshold, and then counts the entire window as mvpa. If value=2 the code looks for a group or groups of epochs with a value above mvpathreshold that span a time window of at least mvpadur minutes in which more than boutcriter percent of the epochs are above the threshold. The motivation for the defition 1 was: A person who spends 10 minutes in MVPA with a 2 minute break in the middle is equally active as a person who spends 8 minutes in MVPA without taking a break. Therefore, both should be counted equal and counted as 10 minute MVPA bout. The motivation for the definition 2 is: not counting breaks towards MVPA simplifies interpretation and still counts the two persons in the example as each others equal. If value=3, using sliding window across the data to test bout criteria per window and do not allow for breaks of 1 minute or longer. If value=4, same as 3 but also requires the first and last epoch to require the threshold criteria."
> >
> > I kept using metric 1 for part 2 to keep GGIR as consistent as possible, while for part 5 I considered it essential that a new bout metric was used. An aspect of part2 is also that it always extracts 6 MVPA bout types which are all independent from each other. This is in contrast with part5 where GGIR spits out MVPA estimates that are complementary, which makes them useful for for example compositional data analysis.
> >
> > Note: you can use argument bout.metric=4 also for part 2, if you prefer this bout.metric.
> >
> > See also previous posts on this topic: https://groups.google.com/d/topic/rpackageggir/GThfLE6xHu4/discussion
> >
> > Best, Vincent
> >
> >

thanks for the input. In fact, I have considered the possibility of night time MVPA, however I didn't expect it to be this significant. Has anyone else come across these differences between part2 and part5?

Best regards,
David

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR: Wear time and sedentary time
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GGIR: Wear time and sedentary time
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrea and Vincent,

just following up on this last reply. Does dur_TINday_min not already include dur_TOINday_min anyway?
The manual says: TIN = Total inactivity = TOIN + TSIB = Total other inactivty + Total sustained inactivity. Why would you add it again?

Regards,
David

Am Sonntag, 10. März 2019 22:13:01 UTC+1 schrieb Vincent van Hees:

> Yes, you probably want to use the sum of dur_TINday_min and dur_TOINday_min.
> Be cautious with calling it sedentary behaviour. GGIR only applies a threshold and does not pretend to classify the activity type sitting.
> I know measuring sedentary behavior is fashion, but realistically wearable sensor methods are generally poor at accurately detecting sitting versus standing activity type. Low acceleration is strongly correlated with sitting time, and that is why you will still see some studies enthusiastically reporting 60-80% accuracy for sedentary behaviour classification. What they really do is measure a correlate of sedentary behavior (defined as sitting and moving little).
> Best, Vincent
>

> On Wed, 20 Feb 2019 at 23:02, Andrea Duran <atdu...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Hi Vincent,
> >
> > Thank you for this information. One more question: which variable do you recommend we use to represent daily sedentary time?
> >
> > As of now, we are using dur_TINday_min from part 5, but I realized that SIB can include daytime sleep. Would dur_TOINday_min be more appropriate (we used a threshold of 50mg to classify sedentary time)?
> >
> > Any feedback is appreciated.
> >
> > Thank you,
> >
> > Andrea
> >
> > On Wednesday, February 20, 2019 at 2:31:57 PM UTC-5, Vincent van Hees wrote:
> > > Hi Andrea,
> > > You will probably be interested in the day specific variables: "nonwear_perc_day", "nonwear_perc_night", and "nonwear_perc_nightandday". Here, "perc" is my abbreviation for percentage.
> > >
> > > Agree that metric ENMO will not inform you about postures. It is in the planning to expand GGIR with the sedentary sphere based classification of 'sitting behaviour (see papers by Alex Rowlands), possibly as optional sub-classes of what we currently call "inactivity" and "sustained inactivity bouts" in GGIR. This may be of value to you. Hopefully I can find time to do this later in the year. The essential signal metrics needed for this are already implemented, main outstanding task is to use them to make the classification.
> > >
> > > As I quite often say in my responses to users: Support with the maintenance and development is always welcome. This can be either financially or in time commitment as motivated here: https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir.
> > >
> > > Best wishes,
> > > Vincent
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On Tue, 19 Feb 2019 at 03:30, Andrea Duran <atdu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > >
> > > > Hello Vincent and fellow GGIR users,
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > I am a PhD candidate in Kinesiology, as well as a new GGIR and R user. The primary outcome of interest for my dissertation is sedentary behavior. I am using the GENEActiv to measure 30 consecutive days of sedentary behavior among an older adult population. I understand that there is some difficulty when distinguishing between postures using the current ENMO metric, but I am primarily interested in the ability of GGIR to detect sleep and non-wear time (as we did not collect sleep diaries from participants).
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Typically, I restrict my analysis to participants that wore the accelerometer for at least 16 hours on at least three days per week over the 30-day period. Then, I look at the association between wear time and total sedentary time to see if I need to correct for the influence of variation in wear time. Therefore, I need to identify which variable represents total duration of wear time at the day level. Based on the data dictionary for part 5, I have identified non-wear time, but it is unclear which variable is duration of wear time at the day level. If possible, can you please direct me to the appropriate data output and variable needed to appropriately restrict participants based on wear time? Any feedback is appreciated.
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Thank you!
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Andrea

Hi Matt,
See argument qwindow that allows you to segment the output per hour of the day.
Further, the milestone data stored in the RData files or optionally

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR: Wear time and sedentary time
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GGIR: Wear time and sedentary time
messages.body_plain:
Yes, David is correct. Sorry, my mistake. TIN = TOIN + TSIB .
So, if you you are interested in total time spent in low accelerations
without the sustained inactivity bouts, but including even very short
blocks of low acceleration in the middle of exercise bouts then use
TOIN.
For the interpretation, however, I think the INB variables (e.g.
dur_INB_D30T30_min) are easier to user.
Regards, Vincent

On Tue, 9 Apr 2019 at 10:27, David <david.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Andrea and Vincent,
>
> just following up on this last reply. Does dur_TINday_min not already include dur_TOINday_min anyway?
> The manual says: TIN = Total inactivity = TOIN + TSIB = Total other inactivty + Total sustained inactivity. Why would you add it again?
>
> Regards,
> David
>
>
> Am Sonntag, 10. März 2019 22:13:01 UTC+1 schrieb Vincent van Hees:
>>
>> Yes, you probably want to use the sum of dur_TINday_min and dur_TOINday_min.
>> Be cautious with calling it sedentary behaviour. GGIR only applies a threshold and does not pretend to classify the activity type sitting.
>> I know measuring sedentary behavior is fashion, but realistically wearable sensor methods are generally poor at accurately detecting sitting versus standing activity type. Low acceleration is strongly correlated with sitting time, and that is why you will still see some studies enthusiastically reporting 60-80% accuracy for sedentary behaviour classification. What they really do is measure a correlate of sedentary behavior (defined as sitting and moving little).
>> Best, Vincent
>>
>> On Wed, 20 Feb 2019 at 23:02, Andrea Duran <atdu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>
>>> Hi Vincent,
>>>
>>> Thank you for this information. One more question: which variable do you recommend we use to represent daily sedentary time?
>>>
>>> As of now, we are using dur_TINday_min from part 5, but I realized that SIB can include daytime sleep. Would dur_TOINday_min be more appropriate (we used a threshold of 50mg to classify sedentary time)?
>>>
>>> Any feedback is appreciated.
>>>
>>> Thank you,
>>>
>>> Andrea
>>>
>>> On Wednesday, February 20, 2019 at 2:31:57 PM UTC-5, Vincent van Hees wrote:
>>>>
>>>> Hi Andrea,
>>>> You will probably be interested in the day specific variables: "nonwear_perc_day", "nonwear_perc_night", and "nonwear_perc_nightandday". Here, "perc" is my abbreviation for percentage.
>>>>
>>>> Agree that metric ENMO will not inform you about postures. It is in the planning to expand GGIR with the sedentary sphere based classification of 'sitting behaviour (see papers by Alex Rowlands), possibly as optional sub-classes of what we currently call "inactivity" and "sustained inactivity bouts" in GGIR. This may be of value to you. Hopefully I can find time to do this later in the year. The essential signal metrics needed for this are already implemented, main outstanding task is to use them to make the classification.
>>>>
>>>> As I quite often say in my responses to users: Support with the maintenance and development is always welcome. This can be either financially or in time commitment as motivated here: https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir.
>>>>
>>>> Best wishes,
>>>> Vincent
>>>>
>>>>
>>>>
>>>>
>>>> On Tue, 19 Feb 2019 at 03:30, Andrea Duran <atdu...@gmail.com> wrote:

>>>>> I am a PhD candidate in Kinesiology, as well as a new GGIR and R user. The primary outcome of interest for my dissertation is sedentary behavior. I understand that there is some difficulty when distinguishing between postures using the current ENMO metric, but I am primarily interested in the ability of GGIR to detect sleep and non-wear time (as we did not collect sleep diaries from participants).

Then, I look at the association between wear time and total sedentary time to see if I need to correct for the influence of variation in wear time. Therefore, I need to identify which variable represents total duration of wear time at the day level. Based on the data dictionary for part 5, I have identified non-wear time, but it is unclear which variable is duration of wear time at the day level. messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

the qwindow option allows you to do that.
see manual:

"To specify windows over which all variables are calculated. If value = c(0,24) all variables will only be calculated over the full 24 hours in a day, If value =c(8,24) variables will be calculated over the window 0-8, 8-24 and 0-24. Previously this functionality was limited to the distribution in acceleration metric values, but now it also derives N valid hours, L5M5 analysis and MVPA."

Regards,
David

messages.subject: Is GGIR for Preschoolers?
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am a new GGIR user. I use wrist-worn actigraph GT9X to measure both preschoolers and parents' physical activity levels. I looked over all the publications that used GGIR, but failed to find anyone used this method to analyze preschoolers PA. I was wondering whether GGIR can be used for preschoolers? In addition, the shell function part 2 and part 5 need to define PA threshold (i.e., lig, mod, vig). So I also wonder whether these thresholds are different between adults and preschool children?

I hope someone can lend your wisdom and advice a bit on these questions. Thank you very much for your time.

Best regards,
Nan

messages.subject: Re: Is GGIR for Preschoolers?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nan,

GGIR can certainly be used in this case, but I am not aware of any specific thresholds with regards to your target group. I personally think, thresholds should not be adapted to every sample unless a lack of sensitivity does not allow to keep the existing ones. This will increase the comparability across different studies and at this stage the thresholds are somewhat arbitrary anyway. The default options worked well for my data. However, some details strongly depend on your research question (for example, would you like to differentiate between long and short bouts). The manual will help you there. I recommend preprocessing your data and comparing the results of different options in order to make an informed decision.

Regards,
David
